title: DIY Home Decor Ideas That Look High-End
h1: DIY Home Decor Ideas: 8 High-End Projects With Materials, Costs and Steps
description: DIY home decor ideas that look store-bought: textured canvas art, plaster vases, fluted furniture and headboards, with materials, costs, time and steps.
excerpt: Eight DIY projects that look expensive, from oversized textured art to a fluted nightstand and upholstered headboard, each with materials, cost, time and steps.
image_alt: Handmade textured canvas art and plaster-effect vases, examples of high end DIY home decor ideas
key_takeaways: Choose projects that mimic high-end materials and shapes: plaster, fluting, upholstery and oversized art.
Most projects cost $10–$150 in supplies and take an afternoon to a weekend.
Prep work, such as cleaning, sanding and priming, is what makes DIY furniture finishes look professional.
Matte, tonal colors and solid metal hardware make handmade pieces look store-bought.
Making objects rather than altering the apartment keeps most DIY decor renter friendly.

faq.q: How can I make my DIY decor look expensive?
faq.a: Copy the materials and proportions of high-end pieces: plaster textures, fluting, upholstered panels and large-scale art. Use matte, tonal colors rather than bright or glossy ones, finish edges and backs neatly, and spend a little more on solid metal hardware and natural fabrics. Thorough prep, including sanding and priming, makes finishes look professional.

faq.q: What is the easiest DIY wall decor?
faq.a: Framed pressed botanicals or fabric and oversized textured canvas art are among the easiest. Both need only basic supplies and no power tools. Textured canvas art uses premixed joint compound and a sample pot of paint, costs roughly $40 to $90 for a large canvas, and takes an afternoon plus drying time.

faq.q: How do you make a vase look like stone or plaster?
faq.a: Mix matte acrylic or latex paint with baking soda until it is about as thick as yogurt, then dab it onto a clean thrifted glass vase with a foam brush. Apply two coats, let it dry, and sand lightly for a weathered finish. The coating is not waterproof, so use dried stems or a glass insert.

faq.q: Is DIY decor cheaper than buying?
faq.a: Usually, especially for large art, upholstered headboards and furniture makeovers, which can cost a fraction of comparable retail pieces. Savings shrink if you need to buy many tools, so choose projects that use basic supplies. Starting from thrifted bases, such as dressers, glass vases and lampshades, keeps costs lowest.

faq.q: What DIY decor is good for renters?
faq.a: Projects that create objects rather than alter the apartment are ideal: canvas art, vases, lampshades, framed botanicals and furniture makeovers all move with you. For headboards or ledges that need mounting, check your lease and ask your landlord, or choose freestanding or leaning options instead.
